=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's Positions and Disclosure Letter

**For:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Scope:** Seller's updated SPA positions (Seller Update) and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003), reviewed against the baseline of 100% of Paperbark Analytics at AUD 24.0m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law.
**Status:** Issues analysis for negotiation planning. Not a substitute for review of the full SPA and data room by NSW-admitted counsel.

## 1. Bottom line

The Seller's package is built to make the Buyer's warranty claims as hard as possible to bring. It does three things at once:

1. **Caps and time-limits everything**, including title and capacity, at general-warranty levels.
2. **Strips out the Buyer's knowledge** through general data room disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2) plus an anti-sandbagging clause (8.3).
3. **Pushes known issues into warranty claims** that the first two points then neutralise.

The disclosed issues are not contingencies to be covered by warranties. They are known, quantifiable items that should be dealt with through price, debt-like adjustments, conditions precedent, and specific indemnities. The Seller's drafting leaves the Buyer to absorb them.

## 2. Liability architecture (SPA cl. 9, 12, 13, 20.5)

| Seller position | Why it hurts the Buyer | Buyer pushback |
|---|---|---|
| General cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m) | The disclosed known items total ~AUD 4.1m in direct cash (see §5). Once they are treated as warranty issues, the cap is nearly consumed before any unknown claim is tested. | Separate caps: general warranties at a materially higher level (open at 100% of price and negotiate down, or at minimum 30–50%, subject to benchmarking). Fundamental and tax warranties at 100% of price. |
| De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k as a deductible (excess only) | A deductible basket on a ~AUD 24m deal (~1%) absorbs the first AUD 250k of loss. Each supplier renewal (AUD 110k) and most individual warranty losses sit below or near the de minimis. | Reduce de minimis to ~AUD 10k and convert to a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once threshold is passed). Exclude specific indemnities from both. |
| General warranty claims: 18-month notice | 18 months is short for tax and for matters like the privacy incident, which may only surface after an audit, complaint, or regulator enquiry. | General: 24–36 months. Tax: statute of limitations plus a buffer (the ATO's standard amendment period is generally four years). Fundamental: 6 years, or the applicable limitation period. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl. 12.3/13) | This is a default-to-the-Seller drafting trick. Every carve-out must be specifically negotiated or it is lost. | Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general warranties, and only where expressly stated. |
| Title and capacity under the general caps and time limits (Fundamental/Title) | The Buyer is buying shares. Title is the core of the asset. A title defect should not be capped at AUD 4.8m or expire at 18 months. | Title, capacity, and authority: capped at price, 6-year (or applicable limitation) period. |
| Exclusive remedy, non-reliance, and limitations apply to all Claims "of any nature" (cl. 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Would purport to cover fraud. A court is unlikely to enforce a contract that shields a party's own fraud in full, but the Buyer should not litigate this. | Express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, and fundamental/title warranties from exclusive remedy, non-reliance, and all caps and time limits. |
| Buyer knowledge bar (cl. 8.3): no claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records | This is anti-sandbagging. Combined with DL 1.1–1.2, it means every disclosed issue, and anything in the data room or public registers, is removed from warranty claims. Advisers' knowledge is also broad. | Delete. Insert a pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's rights are not affected by any knowledge, investigation, or waiver. Under NSW law, the position on knowledge depends on contract construction, so express wording is needed. |

## 3. Disclosure (DL 1.1–1.4; Schedule 7)

- **DL 1.1 and 1.2 are general disclosure of the entire data room (to 5pm 22 Sep 2026) and "publicly searchable corporate records".** This is not acceptable. Disclosure should be specific, fairly disclosed in reasonable detail, and must not operate as a blanket exception to all warranties. Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2 outright and disclose only against specific warranties.
- **DL 1.4 ("nothing admits... any consent... is legally required")** lets the Seller contest whether consents are needed while still being bound to obtain them. The Buyer should require the Seller to obtain specified consents and waivers regardless of legal necessity, as a commercial requirement and CP.
- **The data room cutoff is 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026.** The disclosure is about six weeks stale. Require a bring-down disclosure and an update of the data room as at signing and Completion.
- **Schedule 7 general disclosure reliance** should be struck. The Seller should give a specific disclosure letter only, with all disclosures against specific warranties.

## 4. Specific matters

**Bluefen (DL §2; cl. 3/6.3). High priority.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent under cl. 11.2 is not yet obtained, with conditions under cl. 11.3 outstanding.
- The Seller's wording ("reasonable endeavours"; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent") is weak. Consent should be an unconditional CP, and "satisfied" should require the written consent *and* satisfaction of all cl. 11.3 conditions.
- Specify "all reasonable endeavours" with no obligation on the Buyer to pay consideration or accept adverse terms.
- Set a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right, and consider a price adjustment or escrow if the consent is not obtained or is conditional.
- Ask for a revenue-at-risk analysis. The value impact of losing ~30% of revenue is not addressed anywhere in the Seller's documents.

**Riverlark (DL §3; cl. 2/7). High priority.** The facility is ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, and the Seller proposes a release "following Completion."
- On a debt-free basis, this debt must be repaid from the price *at* Completion, not after. The Buyer should not take on the debt or security even briefly.
- Require: a payout letter with a per-diem; discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations under the *Personal Property Securities Act 2009* (Cth)); release of any guarantees; and a waiver of change-of-control default under cl. 8.1, or confirmation that discharge at Completion resolves it. Discharge documents should be held in escrow pending receipt of payment.
- The funds flow must show the payout amount deducted from the price.

**Employee bonuses (DL §5). High priority.** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are excluded from the funds flow ("a matter for the Seller").
- If the bonuses are paid by the Company post-Completion, the Buyer bears them. They should be treated as transaction-related debt-like items deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller.
- Include employer on-costs. These include superannuation guarantee (currently 12%) and any payroll tax, which the disclosure does not address.
- Confirm the continued-employment conditions and who determines whether they are met.
- Require a reconciled funds flow covering all debt, debt-like, and transaction-related items.

**Ironquay IP (DL §4; cl. 11.1; cl. 7.3 of DD-004). High priority.** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate." The Buyer disagrees:
- Under DD-004 cl. 7.3, Project Materials for SOW3 do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no evidence of payment or a confirmatory assignment.
- Require: evidence of payment from bank records (not the internal ledger); or the Seller pays before Completion; plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay in form and substance satisfactory to the Buyer as a CP.
- Replace the SOW3-limited indemnity with a specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, IP ownership, and licence scope, outside the cap, basket, and de minimis.

**Export/privacy incident (DL §6; DD-006). High priority.** About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may have been sent to an unintended external address. The Seller says the investigation is preliminary and "not expected to be material."
- Business contact details and activity data may still be personal information under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth). If the incident is an "eligible data breach", the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme may require assessment and notification. The Seller should not be the only party assessing this.
- Require: a forensic investigation report before signing, or as a CP; specific indemnity for all costs (investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory response, third-party claims) outside caps and basket; Buyer control or consultation rights over the investigation and any notification; escrow or retention pending outcome; and a warranty on privacy compliance and no prior incidents.
- Time limit for the indemnity should run to at least the end of any regulatory or claims period.

**Office lease (DL §7; DD-007).** The notification obligation is unclear as to landlord consent. Require the lease to be reviewed for change-of-control provisions and, if needed, a landlord consent or estoppel as a CP.

**Supplier renewals (DL §8; DD-008/DD-011; AUD 330k).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs, but the disclosure does not say whether they are terminable or accrued. Read together, they may overlap or extend beyond Completion.
- Confirm terms and termination rights for each renewal.
- Any commitment that is not ordinary-course, or that is entered into between signing and Completion without Buyer consent, should be a pre-Completion liability for the Seller.
- Check whether the AUD 330k affects normalised EBITDA and therefore the valuation.

**Mossvale (DL §9; DD-009).** An assignment restriction exists. Confirm in writing whether the share sale triggers it. If it does, obtain consent as a CP.

**Title (DL §10; DD-012).** The share register is the Seller's evidence of title and is not sufficient on its own.
- Require: certified copy of the register; original share certificates; ASIC company extract; PPSR search over shares; confirmation of no options, rights, or encumbrances over the shares; check of the constitution for transfer restrictions and pre-emptive rights; and board and shareholder approvals.
- Title warranties should be fundamental (see §2).

**Tax and IP (Seller's "settled under the general regime").** Reject. Tax needs its own regime:
- Pre-Completion tax indemnity, with a time limit to statute plus a buffer, outside the general cap.
- Tax warranties at fundamental-level cap and time limit.
- Confirm the NSW duty position on the share transfer. If the Company holds NSW land, landholder duty may apply. Confirm who bears it.

## 5. Known-exposure snapshot

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Current Seller treatment | Buyer treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Release after Completion | Deduct from price at Completion; discharge at Completion |
| Employee bonuses | 420,000 + on-costs | Excluded from funds flow | Debt-like deduction or Seller-paid |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 180,000 | Indemnity limited to SOW3 | Paid pre-Completion or deducted; specific IP indemnity |
| Supplier renewals | 330,000 | "Ordinary course" | Confirm terms; Seller bears pre-Completion commitments; check EBITDA impact |
| Bluefen (revenue at risk) | ~3,600,000 revenue | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfaction | Unconditional CP; long-stop; price/escrow protection |
| Privacy incident | Unquantified | "Not expected to be material" | Specific uncapped indemnity; forensic report; escrow |

Direct cash items (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, supplier renewals) total about AUD 4.13m before on-costs and before any Bluefen value effect. That is close to the Seller's AUD 4.8m general cap. The point is that these should not be warranty claims at all. They belong in the price mechanics and specific indemnities.

## 6. Prioritised recommendations

1. **Reject the general disclosure and anti-sandbagging package** (DL 1.1–1.2, cl. 8.3, Schedule 7). Insist on specific disclosure and a pro-sandbagging clause.
2. **Fix the known items in price and conditions, not warranties**: Riverlark payout at Completion; bonuses and on-costs as debt-like; Ironquay payment and IP assignment as CP; Bluefen consent as unconditional CP with long-stop.
3. **Specific indemnities outside caps, basket, and de minimis** for: privacy incident; Ironquay; bonuses and on-costs; pre-Completion supplier commitments; any Mossvale or lease consent costs; pre-Completion tax.
4. **Restructure liability caps and time limits**: general warranties at a higher cap and 24–36 months; title, capacity, and authority at price and 6 years; tax at price and statute plus buffer; flip the default so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
5. **Carve out fraud** from exclusive remedy, non-reliance, caps, and time limits.
6. **Basket and de minimis**: lower de minimis to ~AUD 10k; tipping basket rather than deductible.
7. **Bring-down** disclosure and data room update to signing and Completion.
8. **Reconciled funds flow** covering all debt, debt-like, and transaction items before signing.
9. **Title verification** per §4.

## 7. Information requests to Seller

- Full data room index and bring-down to current date
- Riverlark payout letter, security list, PPSR search, and change-of-control analysis
- Bank evidence of Ironquay SOW3 payment status; confirmatory IP assignment
- Bonus plan documents, conditions, and payroll tax and super calculations
- Privacy incident log, access logs, investigation scope, and any legal advice on notification (privilege may apply; ask for a non-privileged summary)
- Bluefen cl. 11.2 and 11.3 text, correspondence with Bluefen, and status of conditions
- Supplier renewal contracts (all three), termination terms, and renewal dates
- Lease change-of-control and assignment provisions
- Mossvale assignment clause and confirmation of whether consent is required
- Certified share register, certificates, constitution, and board/shareholder approvals

## 8. Caveats

- Figures and percentages are the Seller's; the Buyer should verify against source documents.
- Recommended cap, time-limit, and basket levels are negotiation openings and must be benchmarked against market data and the Buyer's risk appetite.
- Statutory references (Privacy Act and NDB scheme, PPSA, NSW duties, ATO amendment periods, superannuation guarantee rate) should be confirmed by counsel as at the signing date. Rates and thresholds change.
- The analysis assumes no other documents change the position. The Seller's cover note calls the package "fair and balanced"; that characterisation is not supported by the drafting above.

- Pre-Completion tax indemnity, with a time limit to statute plus a buffer, outside the general cap.
- Tax warranties at fundamental-level cap and time limit.
- Confirm the NSW duty position on the share transfer. If the Company holds NSW land, landholder duty may apply. Confirm who bears it.

## 5. Known-exposure snapshot

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Current Seller treatment | Buyer treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Release after Completion | Deduct from price at Completion; discharge at Completion |
| Employee bonuses | 420,000 + on-costs | Excluded from funds flow | Debt-like deduction or Seller-paid |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 180,000 | Indemnity limited to SOW3 | Paid pre-Completion or deducted; specific IP indemnity |
| Supplier renewals | 330,000 | "Ordinary course" | Confirm terms; Seller bears pre-Completion commitments; check EBITDA impact |
| Bluefen (revenue at risk) | ~3,600,000 revenue | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfaction | Unconditional CP; long-stop; price/escrow protection |
| Privacy incident | Unquantified | "Not expected to be material" | Specific uncapped indemnity; forensic report; escrow |

Direct cash items (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, supplier renewals) total about AUD 4.13m before on-costs and before any Bluefen value effect. That is close to the Seller's AUD 4.8m general cap. The point is that these should not be warranty claims at all. They belong in the price mechanics and specific indemnities.

## 6. Prioritised recommendations

1. **Reject the general disclosure and anti-sandbagging package** (DL 1.1–1.2, cl. 8.3, Schedule 7). Insist on specific disclosure and a pro-sandbagging clause.
2. **Fix the known items in price and conditions, not warranties**: Riverlark payout at Completion; bonuses and on-costs as debt-like; Ironquay payment and IP assignment as CP; Bluefen consent as unconditional CP with long-stop.
3. **Specific indemnities outside caps, basket, and de minimis** for: privacy incident; Ironquay; bonuses and on-costs; pre-Completion supplier commitments; any Mossvale or lease consent costs; pre-Completion tax.
4. **Restructure liability caps and time limits**: general warranties at a higher cap and 24–36 months; title, capacity, and authority at price and 6 years; tax at price and statute plus buffer; flip the default so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
5. **Carve out fraud** from exclusive remedy, non-reliance, caps, and time limits.
6. **Basket and de minimis**: lower de minimis to ~AUD 10k; tipping basket rather than deductible.
7. **Bring-down** disclosure and data room update to signing and Completion.
8. **Reconciled funds flow** covering all debt, debt-like, and transaction items before signing.
9. **Title verification** per §4.

## 8. Caveats

- Figures and percentages are the Seller's; the Buyer should verify against source documents.
- Recommended cap, time-limit, and basket levels are negotiation openings and must be benchmarked against market data and the Buyer's risk appetite.
- Statutory references (Privacy Act and NDB scheme, PPSA, NSW duties, ATO amendment periods, superannuation guarantee rate) should be confirmed by counsel as at the signing date. Rates and thresholds change.
- The analysis assumes no other documents change the position. The Seller's cover note calls the package "fair and balanced"; that characterisation is not supported by the drafting above.
